reference: Data Crystal, The Legend of Zelda/RAM map (GNU FDL 1.2), copied by Logan 2026-10-09; zelda1-disassembly (Aldo Nunez) .dbg

rows.name: frame_counter
rows.notes: Global frame counter in zero page, incremented exactly once per frame (wraps 255->0). Encoding: plain binary, +1 per frame. PROOF/differential search: snapshot, 1 real frame (play_input), snapshot -> 'increased' left 18 hits including 0x0015 37->38; second one-frame round narrowed to 9 hits, 0x0015 38->39; a 60-frame play_input watch on 0x0015 sampled exactly 40,41,...,99 (perfect +1 every frame). Write proof: wrote 0x0015=100, then 30 frames of play sampled 101,102,...,130 - the game incremented from my written value once per frame. NOT the same as 0x0341/0x0342 (a mod-40 animation timer, counts 0-39) or 0x061B-0x061D (short 8/12-frame animation timers).

rows.name: link_facing_direction
rows.notes: Direction Link faces on the overworld. Encoding is a one-hot bitmask: up=$08, down=$04, left=$02, right=$01. Proven by D-pad watch: from a clean start (0x0098=8=up), play_input segments Down/Left/Up/Right with watch on 0x0098 sampled 4,4,...(down) then 2,2,...(left) then 8,8,...(up) then 1,1,...(right) - exactly one value per direction. Sprite confirms: up pose = CHR tiles 12/14, down = 90/8(flip), left = 0/2, right = 4/6 (walking right uses 2/0 with flip_h). WRITE PROOF: wrote 0x0098=1 while the game showed the down pose; after 10 frames Link rendered the right-facing pose (tiles 4/6, screenshot changed) and 0x0098 stayed 1. NOTE: the byte alone does not redraw instantly - the sprite is rebuilt when the main loop processes the direction, so give it a few frames. Companion registers 0x00FA and 0x03F8 carry the same encoding and are the transient render copy (0x00FA drops to 0 while idle); writing 0x00FA=8 immediately flipped the rendered sprite to the up pose (tiles 12/14).

rows.name: game_mode
rows.notes: Game mode / screen-state byte: selects whether the overworld is playing or the item subscreen is up. Observed values: 0 = normal overworld play; 8 = item subscreen fully open; 7,5,2 = subscreen opening animation stages; 9 = subscreen closing animation. Proven by differential search across a Start open/close cycle: snapshot on the overworld (0x00E1=0), press Start, wait ~120 frames -> subscreen displayed and 0x00E1=8 (mid-open it read 7); press Start again, wait ~120 frames -> overworld back and 0x00E1=0 (with a long 9 closing phase). A frame-by-frame watch on 0x00E1 through open+close sampled 0,0,... ->2,5,7,7,...,7 (open) ->8 ->9,9,... ->0. Paired screenshots: overworld with 0x00E1=0, INVENTORY/TRIFORCE subscreen with 0x00E1=8. Note 0x00FC (0-255 ramp) and 0x0026 (3-frame step counter) also change during the transition but are animation counters, not the mode.

rows.name: pause_flag
rows.notes: Game pause flag on the overworld; the game ignores controller input and freezes the action while it is 1. Found by differential search on the first overworld screen (clean start from save state file A): snapshot while playing (0x00E0=0), press Select ~8 frames, wait -> 0x00E0=1 and the diff of the 2KiB was dominated by frame/scratch noise, with 0x00E0 the clean 0->1 bit. Behavioural check: with 0x00E0=1, holding Right 60 frames left Link's X (0x0070) at 120 (frozen). Pressing Select again dropped 0x00E0 to 0 and the same Right hold moved Link (0x0070 120->174). CAUSAL PROOF BY WRITE: from a fresh state (0x00E0=0), wrote 0x00E0=1, then held Right 40 frames -> 0x0070 stayed 120 the whole time and the byte stayed 1 (game did not overwrite it); wrote 0x00E0=0, held Right 30 frames -> 0x0070 climbed 121->160. Distinct from 0x00E1 (game_mode: 0 overworld, 8 item subscreen open). NOTE: the rendered screen is static while paused, so a screenshot cannot confirm pause by itself; the 0x0070 test is the tell. Also note a previous session mapped 0x00FA as a 'render copy' of Link's facing; 0x00FA is actually the controller-1 state byte (see that mapping).

rows.name: controller1_buttons
rows.notes: Player-1 controller state as the game reads it: the held-buttons byte for the current frame. The controller-read routine at CPU $E640-$E678 writes it directly: it latches $4016 (write 1 then 0), shifts 8 reads into a register, then at $E66C-$E676 stores the merged state to 0x00FA,X (X=0 player 1 -> 0x00FA; X=1 player 2 -> 0x00FB). The same routine stores the NEWLY-PRESSED edges to 0x00F8 (player 1) / 0x00F9 (player 2) = current AND NOT previous. Found via trace_writes read on $4016: 1920 reads/120 frames all at PC $E651, then disassembled. PROOF by play_input watch on 0x00FA, one button at a time: Right -> 1 (0x01), Up -> 8 (0x08), A -> 128 (0x80), Select -> 32 (0x20), Start -> 16 (0x10), each held for the full 12-frame press and returning to 0 between presses. Standard LSB-first NES order (A first read -> bit7, Right last -> bit0). NOTE: a previous session mis-recorded 0x00FA as a transient render copy of Link's facing direction; the watch above shows it is the raw controller-1 byte (it equals the direction value only because holding a D-pad sets that bit).
